thread:
sam: Heads-up — p99 on prod-serving-2 climbed from ~220ms to ~600ms starting ~00:45 UTC. Spike correlates with a subset of requests that have very long system prompts and multiple nested tool calls. Logs attached.

lina: Can you paste a short sample of the request/metrics? hoping it's a KV coldstart or a batching weirdness.

sam: sure — excerpt from the prod trace (obfuscated):
```
request_id=abc123\nseq_len=2048\ngen_tokens=512\nkernel_selected=matmul_fused_v2\nbatch_size=3\nmicrobatch_ms=12\nkv_cache_hit_rate=0.38\nkv_warm_latency=42ms\ntool_calls=2->regen_loop\nend_to_end=610ms\np99_bucket=612ms\n```

ben_r: that's interesting — kernel_selected looks fine but kv_hit_rate < 0.4 for long-contexts is bad. Also see microbatch_ms=12 which lets batch grow; on small batches with long kv misses we amplify tail.

jordan: FYI our current adaptive batching policy allows a batch to grow to 8 if backlog appears. for these long prompts, that growth plus KV misses seems to cause multiple kernels to be picked mid-request -> kernel churn.

ops-bot: alert: prod-serving-2 p99 > 500ms for 5m window (service: inference, env: prod). incident-ticket #INC-2026 created.

lina: profiler-bot, can you link the flamegraph for one of these traces?

profiler-bot: artifact: https://ci.internal/profiler/trace/abc123 (flamegraph + open campfire view). quick note: hot path shows repeated re-entry into toolkit.call_handler and repeated KV lookup fallbacks -> stalls in kv_rewarm path.

ben_r: that matches a hypothesis: tool-call loops cause partial generations that hit KV miss, then a regen triggers prefix mismatch, cache gets reallocated — kernel selection logic sees a different sequence length distribution and swaps kernels, which invalidates some CUDA kernels and stalls.

sam: reproduction on staging: send a long system prompt with an async tool that returns structured text (triggering a small re-roll). p99 jumps immediately. put a conservative cap on batch growth and p99 drops ~60ms.

jordan: proposed short-term mitigations: 1) cap adaptive batch growth for requests with seq_len>1024, 2) treat tool-call reentrant requests as "no-batch" by default, 3) pre-warm KV on first token for flagged customers.

lina: long-term: we should add a small state flag that pins kernel selection for the lifetime of a request unless a compatible quantized variant is strictly faster. kernel flips are expensive for long contexts.

ben_r: also add a reentrancy counter and abort after N nested tool calls, or at least force a full context pass (no regen) to prevent oscillation. instrument tool-call depth in metrics.

sam: action items: @ben_r investigate kernel-pin heuristic (estimate: 1.5d), @jordan add batch-cap per-seqlen (0.5d), @lina add KV prewarm flag gating (1d). I'll monitor INC-2026 and post follow-up.

jordan: added minimal config change to staging: `adaptive_batch.max_growth_for_long_seq = 1` — pushed, smoke-green. will run load test.

profiler-bot: load test results: staging p99 for long-prompts down from 420ms to 338ms with batch cap applied. artifacts: https://ci.internal/load/2026

lina: thanks — good incremental wins. we still need the kernel pin before rolling to prod. also let's add an alert: spike in kv_cache_evictions correlated with p99 increase.

sam: noted. closing thread for now — follow-ups in INC-2026 and PRs linked there. if anyone sees regressions after the config roll, ping this thread. :thumbsup:
